correctness.rationale: PASS: For n>=1 independent three-point factors L_i+T_i w+W_i w^2 (nonnegative, summing to 1), assume both parity classes have positive mass. Reconstruct weak Hurwitz stability from each factor, then weak Hermite–Biehler oriented P,Q interlacing for G(w)=P(w²)+wQ(w²); Q/P has nonnegative Stieltjes residues and possible constant term. Deleting a nonpositive real zero (z+x) from P controls modes of the quotient polynomial: x>0 puts every quotient mode at k-1 or k for any P mode k; x=0 permits k-2 through k. Since a nonnegative sum is increasing before the leftmost component modes and decreasing after the rightmost, every Q mode index ℓ is within [k-2,k+1], hence |k-(ℓ+1/2)|<=3/2. All L_i,T_i,W_i>0 forces P(0)>0, deg(Q)<deg(P), so x>0 and zero constant part: ℓ in {k-1,k}, yielding precisely 1/2 separation for every tied-mode choice. G=(1+w)(1+w²)/4 yields sharp 3/2, and L=T=W gives 1/2. One minor algebraic wording imprecision in the prose deletion proof does not alter its strict-unimodality argument. Independent exact coefficient tests 1360 factor cases corroborate; finite cases do not prove all n.
